name: How do ceramic tile and natural stone backsplashes compare for kitchen walls?

mainEntity.name: How do ceramic tile and natural stone backsplashes compare for kitchen walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ceramic and porcelain tiles are generally easier to maintain, while natural stone offers a unique, high-end appearance that requires ongoing care. Ceramic and porcelain come glazed, meaning they resist cooking splatters, grease, and moisture without needing periodic chemical sealers. Natural stone, such as marble or slate, is porous. It absorbs oils and acidic liquids if not sealed regularly. Cutting and installing marble also requires specialized wet-saw work and specific thin-set mortars to prevent staining through the stone, making labor and material costs higher than standard ceramic subway tile.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ceramic tile resists grease and requires zero resealing, whereas natural stone offers distinctive natural veining but demands periodic sealing to avoid stains.
